html:
The Great Lavra is the first and largest monastery on Mount Athos, the mountain peninsula of northern Greece that is still a self-governing community of Orthodox monks. It was founded in 963 by the monk Athanasius the Athonite.

Hermits had lived on Athos before, but Athanasius brought organised community life, with a common rule, a church and shared meals. His friend the general Nikephoros Phokas paid for the building, and grants from later emperors such as John Tzimiskes made the monastery rich. The older hermits at first protested against the change.

Many more monasteries followed, Greek, Georgian, Serbian, Bulgarian and Russian among them, and Athos became the spiritual centre of the Orthodox world. In the 14th century its monks led the hesychast movement, defended by Gregory Palamas. The Lavra still holds a great library of manuscripts, and women have long been barred from the whole peninsula.
